p: The new Bill would amend 784 provisions in 79 Central Acts run by 23 Ministries and replace jail terms with civil penalties for over 1,000 minor offences; fines rise by 10% of the minimum every three years. The 2023 Act had decriminalised 183 provisions in 42 laws.
Method: advice, then warning, then civil penalty. Context: India has 1,536 laws with 69,233 compliances; self-certification instead of affidavits began in 2014.
Challenges: weak deterrence for serious violations and a digital divide (only 24% of rural households have internet).

India's first fully digital census and the 16th overall (8th since independence): Phase I houselisting runs April-September 2026; Phase II population enumeration in February 2027 with caste enumeration; self-enumeration in 16 languages.

First synchronous census was 1881; law is the Census Act 1948 and Census Rules 1990; Census is Entry 69 of the Union List, run by the Registrar General under the Home Ministry; caste has not been fully counted since 1931.

The Bill would raise Lok Sabha seats from 543 to 850 and amend Article 334A to apply one-third women's reservation right after delimitation. It failed to get the two-thirds majority; the Delimitation Bill 2026 and the UT Laws Bill were withdrawn.
It would repeal the Delimitation Act 2002, with a Commission headed by a current or former Supreme Court judge using the 2011 Census; southern and some northern States feared losing weight.

Online Gaming Authority: an MeitY attached office with six members chaired by an Additional Secretary; registration is mandatory for notified games and e-sports; appeals go to the MeitY Secretary; 30 days per level.

AI Governance and Economic Group: 10-member inter-ministerial body of MeitY chaired by the IT Minister, backed by a Technology and Policy Expert Committee; India's AI guidelines have seven sutras (trust, people-centricity, responsible innovation, equity, accountability, understandability, safety-resilience-sustainability).
Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman is elected by the House (Article 89) and acts when the Chairman's office is vacant; a nominated member won the post for the third term running for the first time.

Removal of judges: Articles 124 (SC) and 218 (HC); motion needs 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha signatures; special majority in both Houses; Judges (Inquiry) Act 1968; no judge has been impeached. Recusal is a judge withdrawing for conflict of interest (Ranjit Thakur 1987).

Commonwealth Parliamentary Association: 1911, London, 180 legislatures in 9 regions, journal The Parliamentarian. NCERT: 1961, autonomous, now declared a deemed university by the Centre (on UGC advice); nodal agency for national curriculum frameworks under NEP 2020.

Border 1,751 km across 5 Indian States; India is Nepal's largest export destination; 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship; Nepal accepts UPI since March 2024; Motihari-Amlekhgunj (2019) was South Asia's first cross-border petroleum pipeline; 2024 power deal lets Nepal export 10,000 MW to India over 10 years.

Irritants: Nepal's 2020 map claiming Kalapani, Limpiyadhura and Lipulekh (based on the 1816 Sugauli Treaty and the Mahakali); Nepal joined China's BRI in 2017 after the 2015 blockade; Nepal paused Gorkha recruitment under Agnipath (about 32,000 Nepali soldiers in the Gorkha Regiment).

Links: Integrated Check Posts at Birgunj, Biratnagar, Nepalgunj, Bhairahawa; Kosi (1954) and Gandak (1959) river agreements; Jayanagar-Bijalpura-Bardibas is Nepal's first broad-gauge line; Surya Kiran joint exercise.
The 9th Indian Ocean Conference (India Foundation, started 2016) met in Mauritius with the theme 'Collective Stewardship for Indian Ocean Governance'.

IOR facts: about 36 countries and 35% of world population; 95% of India's trade by volume and 68% by value goes by sea; India's EEZ in the IOR is about 2.4 million sq km; the region carries about 30% of container traffic and 42% of crude oil; cables carry over 95% of global data.

India's frame: MAHASAGAR widens SAGAR beyond the region; Information Fusion Centre-IOR; Operation Sagarbandhu (relief in Sri Lanka after Cyclone Ditwah); AIKEYME (Africa India Key Maritime Engagement); Maritime Security Strategy released April 2026.

ASEAN model: Timor-Leste joined in 2025; Chiang Mai Initiative Multilateralisation is the ASEAN+3 safety net; Digital Economy Framework Agreement. Operation Urja Suraksha: Indian Navy escorts India-bound energy cargoes through the Strait of Hormuz.
RELOS pact with Russia is operational: up to 3,000 troops, 5 warships and 10 aircraft each for 5 years, with reciprocal use of bases and ports (Arctic access for India).
UN Development Partnership Fund (2017, 150 million dollars, India-led, managed by the UN Office for South-South Cooperation) backs LDCs and small island States.

Geography in news: Red Sea (Bab-el-Mandeb to the Gulf of Aden, Suez to the Mediterranean); Qeshm is the largest Persian Gulf island; Scarborough Shoal (China-Philippines); Ust-Luga port on the Gulf of Finland; Malacca Strait (Andaman Sea to South China Sea, about 22% of world trade, narrowest at Phillips Channel); Canary Islands (volcanic, Mount Teide).
Punatsangchhu-II: 1,020 MW run-of-the-river project in Bhutan; tariff protocol signed; the river is a Brahmaputra tributary formed by the Phochhu and Mochhu.
Foodgrain output reached 357.73 million tonnes in 2024-25; agriculture and allied activities make nearly a fifth of GVA at current prices.
The 2026-27 allocation rose to about Rs 1,30,561 crore; schemes include Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses (2025-31) and the National Mission on Edible Oils.

New creditor-initiated insolvency resolution (out of court, for selected financial institutions), a framework for cross-border and group insolvency, a stronger clean-slate rule and a clarification that government dues are not secured creditors for priority.

Timelines: NCLT admits within 14 days of default, decides on resolution plans within 30 days, NCLAT appeals within 3 months, liquidation in 180 days (extendable by 90). The 2019 amendment set 330 days for the whole process.
Record: IBC has resolved 1,376 companies with Rs 4.11 lakh crore recovery; IBBI is the regulator; the 2020 Second Amendment paused CIRP during the pandemic.

Telangana became the fifth State with a gig-worker law (after Rajasthan, Karnataka, Jharkhand, Bihar): a welfare fund from a 1-2% levy on platform transactions, a unique worker ID, penalties for arbitrary rate cuts and a dispute committee for platforms with 100+ workers.

The Code on Social Security 2020 defines gig workers; benefits need 90 days on one platform or 120 across several. Gig workers rose from 77 lakh (FY21) to 120 lakh (FY25), a little over 2% of the workforce; Rajasthan passed the first State Act in 2023.
Safety nets: e-Shram database, PMSBY accident cover of Rs 2 lakh, Ayushman Bharat cover up to Rs 5 lakh for gig workers on e-Shram for 90 days; NITI Aayog suggested a Platform India Initiative.
Proposals: on/off switch for digital payment modes, shared fraud liability between payer's and beneficiary's banks, single-window approval for cross-border payments and full TReDS interoperability.

NPCI (2008 in the source as April 2016 launch of UPI) is a Section 8 not-for-profit set up by the RBI and IBA; UPI grew from about 2 crore transactions (2016-17) to 24,162 crore (2025-26) and banks on UPI from 44 to 703; UPI 123PAY (feature phones), UPI Lite; NIPL (2020) takes RuPay and UPI abroad; Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007 gives RBI power.

Fraud: cases rose from about 2.6 lakh (2021) to about 28 lakh (2025), worth Rs 22,931 crore; ideas: a one-hour cancellable delay for transfers above Rs 10,000 and trusted-person approval for senior citizens' large payments (authorised push-payment fraud is where the victim initiates payment).

Launched 2020: incentives on incremental sales across 14 sectors with Rs 1.97 lakh crore outlay; the food processing PLI drew over Rs 9,000 crore (target Rs 7,000 crore), 69 of 165 approved applicants are MSMEs.

Criticisms: high thresholds shut out small firms, capital-intensive plants create fewer jobs, exports stay in low- and mid-complexity goods, India ranks 44th on the Economic Complexity Index; the House panel wants labour-intensive sectors included.

First report on a calendar-year survey (Jan-Dec 2025): LFPR 59.3% (15+), unemployment 3.1% (urban 4.8%, rural 2.4%), worker population ratio 57.4%, youth unemployment 9.9% (from 10.3%), NEET share 24.9% (15-59).
Shifts: agriculture share of jobs fell from 44.8% to 43.0%; regular wage jobs rose from 22.4% to 23.6%; self-employment fell from 57.5% to 56.2%.
Method: usual status uses the last 365 days, current weekly status the last 7 days, subsidiary status needs at least 30 days of work; PLFS began 2017 and is run by the NSO.

topics.t: Labour codes, edible oils and road safety
p: Four Labour Codes consolidated 29 laws; the Industrial Relations Code allows fixed-term employment, recognises a union with 51% membership as the negotiating union, raises the layoff-approval threshold from 100 to 300 workers and requires 14 days' notice for strikes; labour is on the Concurrent List.

Edible oils: India imports about 56% of its needs; over 70% of oilseeds are rainfed; seed replacement is 25% (groundnut) to 62% (rapeseed-mustard); effective duty on crude oils was raised from 5.5% to 16.5%; committee wants PM-AASHA procurement raised from 25% to 100%, a 'Bharat Oil' brand and a palm oil safeguard duty; NMEO-OS is the oilseeds mission.

Road safety: the Supreme Court (Article 142) read a safe commuting environment into Article 21; NH are about 2% of roads but nearly 30% of deaths; NHAI must place ambulances and cranes every 75 km and patrols every 50 km; district highway safety task forces; no new dhabas in the right of way. The 4Es are Education, Engineering, Enforcement and Emergency care; National Road Safety Strategy runs 2018-2030; only about 25% use seat belts and 50% helmets.

Payments banks (Nachiket Mor Committee, 2014): minimum capital Rs 100 crore, serve the unbanked, keep 75% in SLR securities and 25% with banks. AT-1 bonds are perpetual, can convert to equity in distress and pay higher interest.

RBI barred banks from rupee Non-Deliverable Derivative contracts (cash-settled, traded offshore) and capped banks' Net Open Position in the rupee at 100 million dollars a day; Net Open Position is the gap between foreign-currency assets and liabilities.

Credit default swaps work like insurance on bonds; RBI notified FY27 limits for FPI investment in them. IRDAI brought in an Ind AS-based reporting framework for insurers (Ind AS is the MCA's IFRS-aligned standard).

New Income Tax Act 2025 replaces the 1961 Act: sections cut from 819 to 536, forms from 390 to 190, one 'Tax Year' replaces FY and AY, rates unchanged, virtual digital assets count in undisclosed income. MAT applies to companies, AMT to non-corporates; investments before 1 April 2017 are outside GAAR.
ASISSE: NSO's survey of incorporated service firms (Companies Act or LLP Act 2008) using GST data, about 1.21 lakh units for FY2024-25.
US announced 100% ad valorem duty on patented pharmaceuticals (generics excluded for now); the US takes about 40% of India's pharma exports. Ad valorem duty is a percentage of value.

WTO MC14 (Yaounde): India opposed extending the e-commerce customs-duty moratorium and the IFD agreement; fisheries subsidy talks continue to MC15. Borrowers' Platform (30 founding members, UNCTAD secretariat, chaired by Egypt) is for peer learning, not restructuring.

Forecasts: UN ESCAP sees India at 6.4% this year and 6.6% in 2027 (ESCAP: Bangkok, 1947 as ECAFE); IMF upgraded FY27 to 6.5%; India is 6th in nominal GDP. FAO Food Price Index (base 2014-16; cereals, oils, dairy, meat, sugar) rose to 128.5 in March 2026.
Lithium: KABIL (2019, NALCO, Hindustan Copper, MECL; Ministry of Mines) got clearance for five lithium blocks in Argentina; Argentina, Bolivia and Chile hold over 75% of world lithium.
Land inequality (World Inequality Lab): top 10% of rural households own 44% of land; about 46% are landless; Kerala has the highest land Gini (90); former zamindari areas are more unequal.
Western DFC (Dadri to JNPT, 1,506 km) completed; Eastern DFC runs Ludhiana to Sonnagar (1,337 km); DFCCIL set up in 2006, fully electrified for trains up to 100 km/h.

Urban Challenge Fund: a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Rs 1 lakh crore to unlock Rs 4 lakh crore; 25% of project cost from the fund, at least 50% from market; central guarantee up to Rs 7 crore or 70% of loan in the credit guarantee sub-scheme. PMGSY began 25 December 2000; PMGSY-III extended to March 2028; Phase IV targets 25,000 habitations (62,500 km).

Startup Fund of Funds: Rs 10,000 crore via SIDBI, Empowered Committee chaired by DPIIT Secretary, investing in SEBI-registered AIFs. SASCI: 50-year interest-free loans to States (Mines Ministry Rs 5,000 crore incentive). TDIP scheme 2026-31 backs 5G Advanced and 6G (TSDSI, TCoE India, TCIL). RoSCTL (2019, Textiles, extended to 30 September 2026) rebates embedded taxes; RELIEF under the Export Promotion Mission was widened; Vishwa Sutra (Textiles with NIFT) showcases handlooms.
Defence exports hit Rs 38,424 crore in 2025-26 and production a record Rs 1.54 lakh crore in 2024-25 (DPSUs 77%, private 23%); target Rs 50,000 crore exports by 2029; BrahMos goes to the Philippines.

Draft Defence Acquisition Procedure 2026 raises indigenous content from 50% to 60% for prioritised categories; import bans on over 5,000 items; FDI 74% automatic, 100% with approval for advanced tech; 41 ordnance factories became seven DPSUs.
iDEX and the Technology Development Fund (grants up to Rs 50 crore), SRIJAN portal (2020), 25% of defence R&D for private sector and academia, defence corridors in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

topics.t: AI in internal security and the Mythos risk
p: NCRB's CCTNS 2.0 will use AI to predict Acts and Sections from FIRs; I4C uses Mulehunter.ai to score suspicious transactions and runs a Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit; CDAC Mumbai's tool screens tiplines for child abuse material; SURAKSHINI is a hash bank.
Risks: black-box decisions, bias in training data and unequal internet access (about 45% lack stable access); remedy is human-in-the-loop checks, audits and the DPDP Act.

A panel under the SBI Chairman will assess risks of the AI model Mythos, accessible only to about 40 organisations (Project Glasswing). CERT-In is the incident response agency (MeitY); NCIIPC protects critical information infrastructure.

Third nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (Arihant class, after Arihant and Arighaat) completes India's triad and supports second strike under No First Use; ATV programme began three decades ago with Russian help.

Navy: Malwan (second ASW shallow water craft, Cochin Shipyard), Dunagiri (fifth P17A ship, GRSE), Sanshodhak (fourth large survey vessel), Agray (fourth of eight ASW craft). Tunguska is a Soviet-origin gun-missile air defence system (twin 30 mm guns, 8-10 km); RPSA programme aims at the stealth Ghatak flying-wing UCAV.
IONS: India took the chair in 2026 (rotates every two years); 25 members; table-top exercise held in Kochi. Exercises: Cyclone-IV (India-Egypt Special Forces), Dustlik (India-Uzbekistan).

India is the third-largest renewable producer with 250.52 GW installed; world capacity about 5,150 GW (China about 2,260, US about 470; India ahead of Brazil at 228). Renewables overtook coal in world generation for the first time.

India added 55.3 GW of non-fossil capacity including a record 45 GW solar (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu); 50% non-fossil capacity was reached in June 2025, but non-fossil sources gave 29.2% of generation (538.97 of 1,845.921 billion units).

Risks: imports about 35 million solar modules (1.6 billion dollars) mostly from China, China controls about 90% of rare earth processing, grid evacuation limits (e.g. Tamil Nadu), and over 10 trillion dollars needed by 2070 for net zero.
UNU-INWEH (1996, Ontario) says water bankruptcy is a lasting, irreversible state where use exceeds renewable inflow; water stress is reversible; a water crisis is a sudden shock like drought.
About 70% of major aquifers are declining; over 170 million hectares of irrigated cropland face high stress; the world lost over 30% of glacier mass since 1970.

India has 18% of people but 4% of freshwater; Falkenmark Index: below 1,700 cubic metres per person is stress, below 1,000 chronic scarcity; availability may fall to 1,140 by 2050; about 70% of surface water is polluted.

ABS funds: for identifiable sources 25-40% go to the source institution and 60-75% to communities through State Biodiversity Boards; for traders the money goes to conservation (ABS Regulations 2025). Deep-sea fauna repository Bhavasagara at CMLRE Kochi has over 3,500 specimens; deep sea means below 200 m.

Shekha Jheel (Aligarh, UP) is India's 99th Ramsar site, formed after the Upper Ganges Canal (1852), noted for the Indian river tern and sarus crane. River Basin Management scheme (2014): Rs 2,183 crore for 2026-31, priority to the North East and Indus basin in J&K and Ladakh.

Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules 2026: recycled content rises from 30% (2025-26) to 60% from 2028-29 for Category I; packaging must meet IS 14534:2023. Tar-balls Management Rules 2026 treat tar balls as hazardous waste on a polluter-pays basis.

HFCs (Kigali Amendment 2016): India phases down 10% in 2032, 20% in 2037, 30% in 2042 and 85% by 2047. SAF (waste oil, fats, non-food crops; cuts CO2 up to 80%): 1% for international flights by 2027, 2% by 2028, 5% by 2030 under CORSIA. Flex-fuel vehicles currently run up to E83 and newer designs E100.

Hydro: Kalai-II on the Lohit (Brahmaputra tributary), Kamala on the Kamla (Subansiri tributary). Antarctic: emperor penguin and Antarctic fur seal now Endangered, southern elephant seal Vulnerable (bird flu). CMS COP15 (Brazil, March 2026) launched the Global Taking Initiative (taking threatens about 70% of 1,200 listed species).

Sevilla commitment (UN DESA report 2026) aims to close a 4 trillion dollar yearly SDG gap with 280 actions. Bats: about 135 species in India, 16 endemic, seven threatened. New fanged frog Limnonectes motijheel (Arunachal); gourami fossils in Saharanpur are the first in India and second worldwide (about 5 million years, Pliocene).

AMOC is a current system driven by differences in temperature and salinity (density): dense cold water sinks, flows south on the seafloor and rises again by upwelling. It keeps western Europe milder than Canada or Russia at the same latitude.
Freshwater (melting ice) lowers salinity and density, slowing sinking and weakening AMOC; a collapse could shift the tropical rain belt south and disrupt Indian monsoons.

Graduate unemployment is 29.1%; middle-income household income grew only 0.4% a year; net household financial savings fell to about 5% of GDP; the middle class gives 53% of income-tax filings but is mostly outside welfare nets.

Definitions: OECD middle income is 10-100 dollars a day (PPP); PRICE defines it as Rs 5-30 lakh a year (2020-21 prices). The World Bank international poverty line was revised from 2.15 to 3.00 dollars; lower-middle and upper-middle lines from 3.65 to 4.20 and 6.85 to 8.30.
Supports: income up to Rs 12 lakh effectively untaxed (Budget 2025-26), PM-JAY for all 70+, PMAY-Urban 2.0, SWAMIH fund for stalled projects and RERA.

Artemis II (launched 1 April 2026, about 10 days) was the first crewed Moon mission in 50 years since Apollo 17 (1972): a four-person flyby on the Space Launch System and Orion (NASA with Lockheed Martin), going farther beyond the Moon's far side than any humans; Artemis I (2022) was uncrewed.
Crew: Christina Koch, Victor Glover and Jeremy Hansen of Canada among them, including the first woman, first person of colour and first non-American near the Moon.

Artemis III now becomes a low Earth orbit docking test; Artemis IV (2028) aims to land two astronauts near the lunar south pole. The Artemis Accords (2020, NASA and State Department) reaffirm the Outer Space Treaty and the Rescue Agreement; India is among 67 signatories.

The 500 MW Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (BHAVINI, under the Department of Atomic Energy) attained criticality, advancing stage two of Bhabha's three-stage programme; India will be the second country after Russia with a commercial fast breeder and then move to thorium (India has about 25% of thorium reserves).
Fuel science: U-235 is the only naturally occurring fissile uranium isotope (about 0.7% of natural uranium); Th-232 and U-238 are fertile; Pu-238 powers deep-space missions.

Nuclear Energy Mission (Budget 2025): 100 GW by 2047; nuclear gives about 3% of electricity, capacity 8.78 GW (2024-25); at least five indigenous SMRs by 2033; SHANTI Act 2025 allows limited private participation.
Mahi Banswara project: four 700 MWe PHWRs near Mahi Dam, Rajasthan, by ASHVINI (NPCIL-NTPC), part of fleet-mode 10 identical reactors; AERB was set up in 1983 under the Atomic Energy Act 1962.
Hurdles: India is outside the NSG and NPT; the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act 2010 channels liability; India imports most uranium (Kazakhstan largest) and produced about 500 tonnes in 2024.

One Health links human, animal, plant and environmental health; about 60% of emerging human infections come from animals; the Quadripartite is FAO, UNEP, WHO and WOAH; a global One Health summit was held in Lyon and WHO pushes to end rabies by 2030.

India's mission was approved by PM-STIAC in 2022, anchored by ICMR under the Principal Scientific Adviser's office, with the National Institute of One Health (Nagpur) as anchor institution; NCDC's Centre for One Health runs rabies, zoonoses, leptospirosis and snakebite programmes.

Genome India Project (DBT, 2020): samples from 10,000 healthy unrelated people of 83 groups; tribal groups show high genetic drift and founder effects. Otarmeni is the first gene therapy for OTOF-mutation hearing loss (OTOF codes otoferlin).

DST's post-quantum cryptography roadmap: quantum computers can break RSA and ECC and 'harvest now, decrypt later' threatens stored data. Meghalaya is the third State (after Maharashtra, Gujarat) to partner with Starlink (LEO constellation); DoT licenses, TRAI advises on spectrum, IN-SPACe authorises.

Project Maven (US AI to detect objects in drone imagery) is used in strikes on Iran; Mission MITRA (ISRO with IAF Institute of Aerospace Medicine, at Leh) studies Gaganyaan crew behaviour; cerium-magnesium changesite is the 11th lunar mineral.

Amaravati (Krishna, Guntur) was a Satavahana capital with a legacy to the 3rd century BCE; the Mahachaitya stupa dates to about the 2nd century BCE; early phases show the Buddha symbolically, with human images from the 1st century CE.

Amaravati school (Krishna-Godavari under Satavahanas and Ikshvakus; centres Nagarjunakonda, Amaravati, Goli, Ghantasala, Jaggayyapeta) is one of three main Buddhist art schools with Gandhara and Mathura, known for narrative Jataka scenes.

Nagarjuna is linked to the Madhyamika 'middle way'; Xuanzang came in the 7th century; Kalachakra (Vajrayana) is believed taught here. A Lok Sabha-cleared Bill makes Amaravati the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh.

Jyotiba Phule (born 11 April 1827; Mali family; 'Mahatma' in 1888; Ambedkar's guru) was inspired by Paine's Rights of Man. Works: Tritiya Ratna (1855), Brahmananche Kasab (1869), Gulamgiri (1873), Shetkaryacha Aasud (1883), Sarvajanik Satyadharma Pustak (1891).

Actions: 1848 Pune school with Savitribai as first Indian woman teacher; 1863 home to prevent infanticide; 1868 opened his well to untouchables; Satyashodhak Samaj on 24 September 1873 (marriages without priests or dowry); 1882 memorandum to the Hunter Commission for free compulsory education; member of Poona Municipality 1876-82; he told lower castes to stay away from the Congress.
Savitribai Phule: born 3 January 1831; Mahila Seva Mandal (1852); stipends against dropouts; Kavyaphule (1854); led Satyashodhak Samaj after 1890; died of plague in 1897.
Samrat Samprati: Mauryan emperor, Ashoka's grandson, the 'Jain Ashoka' (texts: Sampratikatha, Parishishtaparvan, Prabhavakacharita); museum opened at Koba, Gandhinagar.

Petroglyphs are rock carvings (Bhimbetka); India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park is being set up on the Indus in Ladakh. Konyaks are the largest Naga tribe, ruled by hereditary chiefs (Anghs), festival Aoleang Monyu; a five-plant polyherbal formulation shows anti-cancer potential.
ADR 2025: 45% of MLAs face criminal cases; Supreme Court scrapped Electoral Bonds in 2024; Vohra Committee studied the crime-politics nexus; ECI seized a record Rs 8,889 crore in 2024.
Theories: virtue ethics (Aristotle), deontology (Kant), consequentialism (Mill), social contract (Rousseau), veil of ignorance (Rawls).

Launched 2016 by restructuring Indira Awas Yojana (1996); Centrally Sponsored under Rural Development; minimum house 25 sq m; assistance Rs 1.2 lakh (plains) or Rs 1.3 lakh (hills, North East, difficult areas); cost sharing 60:40 (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States).

Selection by SECC 2011 housing deprivation data verified by the Gram Sabha; manual scavengers and freed bonded labourers are automatically included; at least 60% for SC/ST and 15% of funds for minorities.
Extras: 90-95 days of MGNREGA labour and Rs 12,000 for a toilet under SBM-G; DBT payments; grievances in 15 days via CPGRAMS.
Progress: original target 2.95 crore houses; 2024-25 to 2028-29 adds 2 crore (total target 4.95 crore); by March 2026 about 4.15 crore allocated, 3.90 crore sanctioned and 2.99 crore completed.
